Retail Workers Stage Nationwide Walkout, Disrupting Stores Across Austria

A nationwide walkout by retail workers has brought widespread disruption to shops and supermarkets throughout Austria, as staff at hundreds of outlets left their posts on Thursday morning. The strike, which union leaders say involves more than 30,000 employees, is the largest industrial action the sector has seen in a decade.

The Austrian Retail Workers’ Union called the strike after negotiations over pay and working conditions broke down for the third time this spring. "Retail staff have worked tirelessly through recent years but have seen little improvement in wages or conditions," said Renate Berger, the union’s spokesperson. "Our members want fair compensation and respect for their essential role."

Stores operated by major chains such as Alpenmarkt, Stadtkauf, and KonsumPlus reported closed doors or skeleton crews at multiple locations, particularly in Vienna, Linz, Salzburg, and Graz. Shoppers arriving at outlets found locked entrances and signs explaining the situation, while some city centre branches operated with limited staff and reduced hours.

"We are unable to open as usual," said a manager at a Stadtkauf branch in Innsbruck. "Only a handful of team members have come in, and shelves are not being restocked."

Industry analysts estimate that up to 60% of outlets in the sector are currently affected. "This is a significant blow for retailers in the midst of the busy early summer period," commented Martin Weiss, an industry consultant. "Losses could reach several million euros per day if the action continues."

Retail workers, many picketing outside stores with banners reading "Fair Pay Now," say they are prepared to continue the walkout until an improved offer is made. Negotiations are reportedly set to resume on Friday, but as of Thursday afternoon, no agreement had been reached.

Union officials have urged the public for understanding, stating, "Our fight is for dignity and fairness—principles that benefit everyone in the industry."
